blocks.text: 1 Samuel 19 contains 24 verses. It opens with: And Saul spake to Jonathan his son, and to all his servants, that they should slay David. But Jonathan, Saul's son, delighted much in David. It concludes with: And he also stripped off his clothes, and he also prophesied before Samuel, and lay down naked all that day and all that night. Wherefore they say, Is Saul also among the prophets? Supplied contextual evidence for this passage adds: The book explicitly attributes a harmful spirit affecting Saul to the LORD after the Spirit of the LORD departs; medical, psychological, spiritual, and theological explanations should not be collapsed into one diagnosis.
